title: Home brew and Shots Madison
summary: Bailey describes making home brew; the interviewers mention Shots Madison selling it in Prohibition.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: They were going to get it during the morning. They make their own beer. Yeah, make their own beer. Any of them have skills? Did they do any distilling through moonshine?

No, we used to make it too, at all. I don't know. We'd make it, put it up, and have to leave it for four or five days, then you go to put it in your bottle. You get a cap, then after you put it in the bottle, you leave it there for about... Well, some folks leave it for a day, and then they go to say, light the cap to that evening to drink it.
Somebody told me once that Shots, did you know Shots Madison or Kid Shots? That was a, he used to sell homebrew. That was his main job, I think, during Prohibition. Yeah. But Fess told us. Yeah.
Well, you know, Kid Ernest was in that sometimes too.
Did you know Shots, he was uptown.
He lived in the battlefield. Yeah.
He lived up on Cleveland. Yeah, I know the battlefield.
He played in all the parades, and not all of them a lot of times.
Yeah. Yeah, we used to make it. Good beer, homebrew. Take time to make it, but when you make it, you enjoy it.
